To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
fast DKI combined with ICON analysis provides improved characterization of heterogeneous DWI lesion in stroke.

fast diffusion kurtosis with ICON analysis enhances automatic segmentation of DWI stroke lesions, and that the ratio of kurtotic to diffusive lesion volumes is a promising metric to characterize the extent of irreversible tissue injury.

fast DKI kurtosis imaging, with Inherent C‐based Normalization, enables automated segmentation of heterogeneous diffusion‐weighted imaging stroke lesions in rats, and that the relaxation‐normalized kurtosis lesion volume was 2.5 times larger than the diffusivity‐normalized volume.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new imaging biomarker, RNMK, to enhance the specificity and accuracy of stroke lesion delineation.
a new method of DKI data analysis, which is based on the inherent correlation between the kurtosis and relaxation parameters.
the development of a new MRI technique that can be used for improved diagnosis and treatment of acute stroke.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
fast DKI combined with ICON analysis provides promising means of demarkation of heterogeneous DW‐hyperintense stroke lesions.
fast diffusion kurtosis with inherent correlation‐based normalization (ICON) analysis is an effective means of demarcating heterogeneous ischemic tissue in stroke.
ICON‐DKI can be used to enhance automatic segmentation of heterogeneous ischemic lesions in stroke.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ICON analysis enables automated segmentation of heterogeneous ischemic lesions and provides a means for improved definition of irreversible ischemia in stroke.
DKI can be used to detect and quantify ischemic tissue injury, and that ICON analysis enhances DKI's specificity for ischemia.
DKI can provide a more sensitive measure of tissue injury, but the kurtosis values are heterogeneous.
The main takeaway from our work is that
fast DKI combined with ICON analysis can be used for automated segmentation of heterogeneous stroke lesions, providing an important tool for the study of acute stroke.
the proposed ICON analysis can be applied to fast DKI data for improved characterization of ischemic tissue injury.
ICON‐DKI may provide an improved means of delineating acute ischemic lesions in the brain.
